gate3CanaryAttempt.suspectedRootCause: The handler's worker.py enforces TORCH_FORCE_WEIGHTS_ONLY_LOAD=1 before any weight is loaded (enforce_safe_load) and exits with a non-JSON-producing failure path if it is unset; the canary's template was created with an empty env object ({}), so this required environment variable was never set on the worker. This is a plausible, code-derived explanation for the observed failure shape (ok=false, no gpu field, no providerPostCount field, matching the handler's generic _safe_error fallback for a non-JSON subprocess result) but is not independently confirmed, because the job/worker/endpoint were deleted by mandatory cleanup before raw stdout/stderr could be retrieved. Confirming this requires a new, separately authorized diagnostic step (e.g. a template env fix plus a new explicit Gate 3 approval) before another canary may run.

offlineRootCauseAnalysis.authorization: read-only repository/image inspection only; anonymous image pull by digest; no RunPod/S3 call; no dispatch
offlineRootCauseAnalysis.evidenceSummary: TORCH_FORCE_WEIGHTS_ONLY_LOAD=1 is already baked into the published image's Config.Env (verified via anonymous GHCR Docker Registry HTTP API v2 manifest/config inspection of digest sha256:29ca5aa0aae46ab03719c52ae25fa98a61830adbbc8b317bd244ffb7ff837d9b); handler.py's subprocess.run() call passes no env= override, so the CLI worker subprocess inherits the full container environment by default. An empty RunPod template env could not have removed an already-baked image ENV entry under standard OCI/Docker container-runtime semantics.
offlineRootCauseAnalysis.realRootCauseStatus: unconfirmed -- mandatory cleanup deleted the job/worker/endpoint before any log-retrieval call was authorized; RunPod's job status API exposes no stdout/stderr endpoint

gate3CanaryAttempt2.diagnosticFinding: The improved sanitized diagnostics (added in PR #85) captured errorDetail='worker exited with unexpected code 1' for the first time -- this is handler.py's generic RuntimeError message for a CLI worker subprocess exit code outside (EXIT_OK=0, EXIT_INPUT=2, EXIT_WEIGHT=4, EXIT_CUDA=5). Exit code 1 is worker.py's EXIT_INTERNAL, its catch-all for an unclassified/uncaught exception in main(). This positively rules out the EXIT_WEIGHT (missing/invalid weight) and EXIT_CUDA (no CUDA available) failure paths specifically -- if either had occurred, the exit code would have been 4 or 5, not 1 -- which is further confirmation that the env-var hypothesis from run 30691401701 was correctly classified CONTRADICTED. The exact Python exception/traceback remains unavailable: worker.py prints 'internal error: {e}' to its own stderr, which handler.py's subprocess.run() call does capture (stderr=subprocess.PIPE) but does not include in the RuntimeError message or the JSON response returned to the RunPod job API -- so this specific stderr text was never retrievable from the job status response, and mandatory cleanup deleted the worker before any other retrieval path existed.
gate3CanaryAttempt2.followUpRootCauseRecord: docs/restoration/runpod-restore-unpack-fix-candidate.json -- offline analysis (2026-08-01, no RunPod call) classified EXIT_INTERNAL as ROOT_CAUSE_CONFIRMED: worker.py's _run_restore() unpacked GFPGANer.enhance()'s verified 3-tuple return into only 2 variables, raising an uncaught ValueError on every successful restore call. Fix applied only in a new unpublished candidate (apps/api/runpod-worker-gpu-dev-restore-unpack-fix/); the approved/published image is unchanged.

The evidence script's productionRoutingAllowed default ('// true' fallback used when no .output object exists at all) printed 'true' in the raw log for this run; this is a diagnostic-default artifact, not evidence that production routing occurred -- no job execution happened at all, and productionRoutingAllowed is not part of the success-gate's own pass/fail logic.

gate3CanaryAttempt4.diagnosticFinding: This is a new, different failure mode than any prior canary: the job reached IN_PROGRESS (unlike run 30699352406, which stayed IN_QUEUE for the full 120s and was cancelled) and ran for approximately 9.6s of billed execution time before the handler returned errorDetail='worker produced invalid non-JSON output' -- distinct from the earlier 'worker exited with unexpected code 1' (EXIT_INTERNAL) signature seen in runs 30691401701/30692613631, which were traced offline to the GFPGANer.enhance() unpack bug and already fixed in the currently-deployed corrected image. Because this canary used that corrected image and still failed, with a different error signature, the corrected worker.py's restore path remains unconfirmed under real GPU conditions; the exact cause of 'invalid non-JSON output' (e.g. a subprocess stdout/stderr interleaving issue, a different runtime exception, or a CLI-worker output-format mismatch) was not diagnosed in this task -- root-cause analysis was out of scope for this approval, which authorized exactly one dispatch and evidence capture only, not further debugging or a second dispatch. Cost was well within budget ($0.001538 of $0.05); FlashBoot was requested and the response confirmed flashboot=true this time (unlike the schema-only omission case anticipated for endpoints that do not return the field), and the worker took 74s to first reach ready, longer than in prior runs, consistent with the corrected image's ~6.75GB size and normal cold-start variability rather than any change caused by requesting FlashBoot on this single data point.
